newsitem.title: USA: Wall St stocks power higher as more records fall.
newsitem.headline: Wall St stocks power higher as more records fall.

text.p: The Dow industrials charged to yet another record on Wednesday as momentum in blue chips continued to build, prodded onward by falling interest rates.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 32 points to about 6430, for its first close above the 6400 mark and tenth record this month. Caterpillar Inc led the rally and was one of several components to hit a new high for the year.
"There's no question it's frothy but this is sustainable as long as bond yields stay to the market's advantage," said Joseph Battipaglia, chief investment officer at Gruntal & Co.
Market breadth was moderately positive, with advancing issues outnumbering decliners by about four-to-three on heavy New York Stock Exchange volume of about 494 million shares.

The session was a choppy one that saw stocks burst higher at the open and falter when bonds failed to rally. However, a successful afternoon auction of $12.5 billion in five-year U.S. notes raised morale and sent the 30-year bond up 12/32 to push the yield down to 6.41 percent.
"If you made a model of what drives the market, you'd have to say none of the variables is changing except bond yields," Battipaglia said.

However, despite the fact that several indices established record highs on the session -- among them the NYSE Composite and Standard & Poor's 500 -- the Dow once again outperformed the broader market, extending a trend that has raised caution on Wall Street.

Among those raising yellow flags was Prime Charter Ltd Chief Investment Strategist Scott Bleier, who decreased the amount of stocks and bonds in his firm's asset allocation model, citing the recent run-up in prices.
"We feel that the activity in the first-tier, largest capitalized names has reached frenetic levels," Bleier said.
Bleier also said of stocks that "the narrowness of their advance is cause for near-term concern."

Despite mounting caution, investors showed sustained desire for any blue chip stock that appears poised to outperform. Caterpillar was one such stock, surging 4-3/4 to 78-3/4 after Smith Barney upgraded the shares to buy.

"There's so much money still waiting to get in on any reason," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Van Kampen American Capital. "Any move from a hold to a buy has the potential to move a stock like this."
Boeing Co climbed 2-3/8 to 96-3/8 after reports that AMR Corp unit American Airlines was set to place a multi-billion aircraft order.

Shares in AMR, which declined to comment on the report, fell one point to 91. After the close of trading, the union representing AMR's pilots said its board approved a tentative labor pact with the company. AMR has long maintained it would not buy any aircraft until reaching such a labor agreement.
General Motors Corp rose 2-1/2 to 57-1/8 amid rumors its Hughes Electronics Corp unit might merge with Raytheon Co.
Shares in Hughes, which trade separately from GM, jumped 3-3/4 to 53-1/2 and Raytheon gained 2-1/2 to 52-3/8. All three companies declined to comment on the rumor.
Revlon Inc fell 3-1/2 to 30-1/8 after Smith Barney trimmed its fiscal 1997 earnings estimate on the company to $1.10 per share from $1.18.
The S&P 500 index rose 1.79 to 743.95 and the NYSE Composite gained one point to 392.80, both records.
